LESSON: DIVISION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.6: Division
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Division, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: how many How can you share a given number of objects equally?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in purposive teams or pairs to share a given number of objects equally by each picking one object at a time using any functional part of the body/ appropriate Assistive technology for manipulation with physical support until all the objects are finished. Each learner to count

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in purposive teams or pairs to share a given number of objects equally by each picking one object at a time using any functional part of the body/ appropriate Assistive technology for manipulation with physical support until all the objects are finished. Each learner to count

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Division together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learner learns to organise numbers up to 25 into groups of 4 or 5 without a remainder,

● Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving division.

Values:
● Love: learner shares a given number of objects equally by each picking one object at a time until all the objects are finished.

● Unity: learner works harmoniously in teams as they place objects together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Positive discipline: learner works harmoniously in teams as they place and share objects together.

● Social cohesion: learner plays games involving division using digital devices or other resources with peers.

Link to other learning areas:

● The learner relates the skills of writing division statements to functional writing in English Language Activities.

● The learner relates the concept of equal sharing to the concept of values in Religious Activities.
